skill.name: linear
skill.description: Manage Linear issues, teams, projects, comments, links, and GraphQL workflows through the Linear CLI.
skill.summary: Use the Linear CLI from AI agents to manage issues, projects, teams, and GraphQL tasks.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples for Linear CLI and GraphQL usage, not executable backtick code. Confirmed issues involve credential exposure, prompt-injection-like QA instructions, and forced-confirmation examples for destructive Linear mutations. The author should harden documentation around secrets, local config, and user approval before publication.

remediation.issue: QA.md includes prompt text that directs agent behavior during review.
remediation.suggestion: Move QA prompts outside the packaged skill or label them as inert examples that must not override system instructions.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance can reveal Linear credentials through raw config output or external web headers.
remediation.suggestion: Use redacted auth commands, avoid cat on config files, and warn users not to paste API keys into third-party tools.

remediation.issue: Examples use --yes with create, update, link, delete, and project mutation workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before every mutating command and separate destructive archive examples from routine workflows.

remediation.issue: GraphQL recipes use fixed /tmp filenames for query and response files.
remediation.suggestion: Use unique temporary filenames and delete response files that may contain signed upload URLs or workspace data.

Interacts with Linear for issue tracking and project management using the `linear` command.
- Use for Linear issue/project/teams management via the CLI or GraphQL (`linear gql`).
- Defaults: `linear config set default_team_id TEAM_KEY`, `linear config set default_output json|tab
- Inspect or reset defaults: `linear config show`, `linear config unset default_output`
- **Branches**: Name as `{TICKET}-{short-name}` (e.g., `ENG-123-fix-auth`); prefer git worktrees for
- **Assignment**: Assign yourself when starting work (`linear issue update ENG-123 --assignee me --y
- **Sub-issues**: Set parent to associate related work (requires UUID: `linear issue update ENG-123
- **Scope creep**: Create separate issues for discovered work; link with blocks relation (`linear is
| `linear issues list` | List issues with filters |
| `linear issue view ID` | View single issue |
| `linear issue update ID` | Update issue (assign, state, priority, parent*) |
| `linear issue link ID` | Link issues (blocks, related, duplicate) |
| `linear issue comment ID` | Add comment to issue |
| `linear issue delete ID` | Archive an issue |
| `linear project view ID` | View project details |
| `linear project update ID` | Update project (state, name, dates) |
| `linear project delete ID` | Archive a project |
| `linear project add-issue` | Add issue to project |
| `linear project remove-issue` | Remove issue from project |
*`--parent` requires UUIDs, not identifiers. See [Finding IDs](#finding-ids).
- `--team ID\|KEY` - Specify team (required for most commands)
**Note:** `--parent` requires UUIDs. Get UUID with `linear issue view ID --json | jq -r '.issue.id'`
- [ ] List teams to get TEAM_KEY: `linear teams list`
- [ ] Create parent issue: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Epic" --yes`
- [ ] Create child issue: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Task" --yes`
- [ ] Get parent UUID: `linear issue view PARENT_ID --json | jq -r '.issue.id'`
- [ ] Set parent (UUID required): `linear issue update CHILD_ID --parent PARENT_UUID --yes`
- [ ] Create another issue to link: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Blocked" --yes`
- [ ] Link blocking issue: `linear issue link ISSUE_ID --blocks OTHER_ID --yes`
| Empty results | No team specified | Add `--team TEAM_KEY` |
| 401 Unauthorized | Invalid/missing API key | Run `linear auth test` |
| Mutation does nothing | Missing confirmation | Add `--yes` flag |
| Can't find issue | Wrong ID or missing access | `issue view` accepts identifier or UUID; verify sp
| --parent fails | Using identifier | `--parent` flag requires UUID, not identifier |
**ID format summary:** Most commands accept identifiers (ENG-123). Exception: `--parent` requires UU

content.user_title: Manage Linear Issues from AI Agents
content.value_statement: Teams lose time moving between chat, code, and Linear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Linear CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists and searches Linear issues, teams, and projects with CLI filters.
Creates, updates, links, comments on, and archives Linear issues.
Returns JSON or selected fields for agent-friendly issue analysis.
Provides GraphQL recipes for attachments, uploads, relations, parents, and assignment.
Documents troubleshooting for authentication, configuration, GraphQL, and connection errors.
limitations: Requires the Linear CLI to be installed and available on PATH.
Requires a valid Linear API key or configured local authentication.
Mutating commands affect the real Linear workspace and need user approval.
Raw GraphQL workflows require correct UUIDs and Linear schema knowledge.

use_cases.title: Triage assigned work
use_cases.description: List open issues, inspect details, and summarize next actions for a personal queue.

use_cases.title: Plan linked delivery work
use_cases.description: Create parent tasks, child tasks, blockers, and comments during sprint planning.

use_cases.title: Validate Linear automation
use_cases.description: Test CLI commands, GraphQL recipes, file uploads, and authentication behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Show my open work
prompt_templates.prompt: List my open Linear issues for TEAM_KEY. Summarize identifier, title, state, priority, assignee, and URL.

prompt_templates.title: Create a tracked task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Linear issue in TEAM_KEY titled "TITLE". Ask before using confirmation flags or changing workspace data.

prompt_templates.title: Organize related issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a parent issue and two child issues, then link the blocker relationship after I approve each mutation.

prompt_templates.title: Run a GraphQL workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Linear GraphQL to attach a URL to an issue. Resolve required UUIDs first and show the planned mutation before running it.

output_examples.input: List my current Linear issues for the engineering team.
output: The assistant identifies the team, lists open assigned issues, and groups them by state.
Each result includes the issue identifier, title, priority, assignee, and Linear URL.

output_examples.input: Create a bug task and link it as blocking an existing issue.
output: The assistant asks for approval before creating or linking issues.
After approval, it reports the new issue identifier and the confirmed blocker relationship.

output_examples.input: Help me debug a Linear authentication failure.
output: The assistant checks authentication status with redacted output and suggests safe setup steps.
It avoids printing API keys or raw local configuration contents.

best_practices: Confirm the target workspace, team, and issue identifiers before any mutation.
Prefer built-in Linear CLI commands before using raw GraphQL recipes.
Use redacted authentication checks and avoid printing API keys or config files.
anti_patterns: Running confirmation flags for create, update, link, or delete actions without user approval.
Copying Linear API keys into shared prompts, logs, screenshots, or web tools.
Using raw GraphQL when a documented CLI command provides the same operation.

faq.question: Does this skill install the Linear CLI?
faq.answer: No. It documents CLI workflows. The Linear CLI must already be installed.

faq.question: Does it need a Linear API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Authentication must be configured through the CLI or a safe environment variable.

faq.question: Can it create or update real issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Any mutation should be reviewed and approved before execution.

faq.question: Can it use GraphQL directly?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes recipes for operations not covered by built-in commands.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The content is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use redacted auth commands. Do not print API keys or raw config files.
